territorial_scope.description: Applies in all EU Member States; obligations fall on public sector bodies holding the listed datasets.

evidence.quote: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

summary.short: Lists specific high-value datasets in six thematic categories and requires public sector bodies holding them to publish them for re-use via APIs, under open licences (CC0 or CC BY 4.0), from 16 months after entry into force.
summary.long: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/138 lays down a list of specific high-value datasets under Directive (EU) 2019/1024, in six thematic categories (geospatial; earth observation and environment; meteorological; statistics; companies and company ownership; mobility), with granularity, key attributes, formats and update frequencies set in the Annex. Public sector bodies holding listed datasets must make them available for re-use in machine-readable formats via APIs, with bulk download where the Annex requires it, publish API terms of use, quality of service criteria and documentation, designate an API point of contact, and mark the datasets as high-value in their metadata (Art. 3). Art. 4 requires re-use under CC0 or CC BY 4.0 or an equivalent or less restrictive open licence, applies the obligations to existing machine-readable high-value datasets created before the date of application, and requires publication of Member State exemptions granted under Directive 2019/1024. Member States must report on implementation within two years of entry into force, then every two years on request, including the number of exempted bodies (Art. 5). Binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States, it applies 16 months after entry into force (Art. 6).

thresholds.note: The operative provisions (Articles 1-6 and Annex sections 1-6) set no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Numbers found are technical specifications (scale 1:5 000, update frequencies, formats), statistical definitions in Annex tables (e.g. poverty and work-intensity measures), or procedural time limits (Art. 5 reporting, Art. 6 application date, coded as events). The two-year exemption period appears only in recital (6), which is not an operative provision, and Article 4(1) refers to the exemption without a period. Any cutoffs governing the free-of-charge exemption sit in Directive (EU) 2019/1024 Art. 14, which this Regulation implements.
